lines.trans: We need to find something new in France.
I think we do not need to change anything yet.
Stop it, we have a modern restaurant after all!
We must always move only forward.
There is so much good and beautiful around right now.
We need to remove the old and not regret it.
Vika, what do you think about this yourself?
No, friends, you have written me off too soon!
Come on, work faster in my kitchen!
Right now your chef is going to cook himself!
Why did he decide to cook before dinner?
Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.
Give it here, I will make everything myself!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Почему это нельзя кричать на тебя?
examples.trans: Why is it that I cannot shout at you?

examples.text: Почему вы ему ничего не сказали?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell him anything?

examples.text: Почему он решил готовить до ужина?
examples.trans: Why did he decide to cook before dinner?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Рождаются миллионы новых людей.
examples.trans: Millions of new people are born.

examples.text: Ведь уже скоро лето закончится.
examples.trans: After all, summer will end soon.

examples.text: Макс, откуда он здесь взялся?
examples.trans: Max, where did he come from here?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Почему он решил готовить до ужина?
examples.trans: Why did he decide to cook before dinner?

examples.text: Нет, я просто решила его проучить.
examples.trans: No, I simply decided to teach him a lesson.

examples.text: Ты решил забрать мою работу, старый друг?
examples.trans: Did you decide to take my job, old friend?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты уже стареешь, дорогой Витя?
examples.trans: Are you getting old already, dear Vitya?

examples.text: Раньше ты так долго не думал.
examples.trans: Before, you did not take this long to think.

examples.text: Что тебе надо? Ничего, работаем.
examples.trans: What do you want? Nothing, we are working.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Почему он решил готовить до ужина?
examples.trans: Why did he decide to cook before dinner?

examples.text: Романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: A romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на ужин?
examples.trans: What do we have for dinner today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот какой хитрый наш шеф!
examples.trans: What a sly chef we have!

examples.text: Вот новый заказ для Дмитрия Владимировича.
examples.trans: Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Вот смотри, на меня тоже вода попала.
examples.trans: Here look, water got on me too.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ведь уже скоро лето закончится.
examples.trans: After all, summer will end soon.

examples.text: Вот новый заказ для Дмитрия Владимировича.
examples.trans: Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Макс, можешь уже заканчивать этот спектакль.
examples.trans: Max, you can end this performance already.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Для него это очень скучное место.
examples.trans: For him this is a very boring place.

examples.text: Вот новый заказ для Дмитрия Владимировича.
examples.trans: Here is a new order for Dmitry Vladimirovich.

examples.text: Дмитрий Владимирович, шеф сам для вас готовит.
examples.trans: Dmitry Vladimirovich, the chef is cooking for you himself.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: Хорошо, я буду ждать вашей правды.
examples.trans: Alright, I will wait for your truth.

examples.text: Почему гость должен так долго ждать?
examples.trans: Why must the guest wait for so long?

examples.text: Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катя тоже недавно вернулась сюда.
examples.trans: Katya also recently returned here.

examples.text: Сейчас я позову Катю сюда.
examples.trans: I will call Katya here right now.

examples.text: Катя, иди скорее сюда ко мне!
examples.trans: Katya, come here to me quickly!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В мире всё всегда меняется.
examples.trans: Everything in the world always changes.

examples.text: Ты когда приехал? Пойдём, всё расскажешь.
examples.trans: When did you arrive? Let us go, you will tell me everything.

examples.text: Лучше я сама ему всё скажу.
examples.trans: It is better if I tell him everything myself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will do', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Витя, когда ты сделаешь новое меню?
examples.trans: Vitya, when will you make the new menu?

examples.text: Дай сюда, я всё сам сделаю!
examples.trans: Give it here, I will make everything myself!

examples.text: Прости, я сейчас быстро всё сделаю.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I will quickly make everything again right now.

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will prepare', paired with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Что ты приготовишь, когда ты так устал?
examples.trans: What will you cook when you are so tired?

examples.text: Я торт приготовила.
examples.trans: I made a cake.

examples.text: Мама приготовила вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the best').

examples.text: Лучше я сама ему всё скажу.
examples.trans: It is better if I tell him everything myself.

examples.text: Хватит спорить, лучше готовься к свадьбе!
examples.trans: Enough arguing, you had better get ready for a wedding!

examples.text: Я приготовлю лучшее блюдо!
examples.trans: I will cook the best dish!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Зачем людям летом новые блюда?
examples.trans: Why do people need new dishes in summer?

examples.text: Я приготовлю лучшее блюдо!
examples.trans: I will cook the best dish!

examples.text: Я тебе сейчас новое блюдо приготовлю!
examples.trans: I will cook a new dish for you right now!
